How do I ping this check?

Have your job call the URL above when it runs — a plain GET or POST reports success. Add a suffix for other signals:

SignalURLEffect
successhttp://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9marks the check up
failhttp://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/failmarks the check down
starthttp://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/startopens a run so an overrun can be caught
loghttp://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/logrecords a note, status unchanged
exit codehttp://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/<code>0 = up, anything else = down
shell examples# report success when the job finishes curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9 # wrap a job: start it, run, then report the exit code curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/start mybackup.sh curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/$? # report failure and attach the output (shown in Recent pings) mybackup.sh 2>&1 | curl -fsS --data-binary @- http://localhost:18080/ping/cc1160bb-1da8-42d0-add2-4d2ebee414a9/fail
oldersolid = timed run, taller = longer · hollow = duration not measurable · amber ≥80% budget · red = failednow
